<message>
My father has dementia and he does not recognize me anymore. That makes me sad beyond measure.
</message>

<passage>
To my will the will of another is as indifferent as his poor breath and flesh. And how much soever we were formed for the sake of each other, yet the governing part of each of us has its own proper power; otherwise the vice of another might become my own misery. God thought fit that this should not be; lest it should be in another's power to make me unhappy.
</passage>

output.reason: The passage emphasizes inner resilience and not being controlled by others' actions, which may feel dismissive of grief over a loved one's illness.
